column3: 2. Promote the restoration of degraded ecosystems [within protected areas and other effective area-based conservation measures, recognizing indigenous and traditional territories, where applicable], and beyond, including buffer zones, ecological corridors, soil biodiversity[, [including] fungal biodiversity,7] and inland water ecosystems, with a view to restoring ecological integrity and ecological connectivity across landscapes and seascapes, including through the development of criteria for identifying priority restoration areas and approaches for measuring restoration success, ensuring inclusive and gender-responsive implementation of the restoration efforts, as appropriate. [2.bis Scale up ecological connectivity measures within currently under-represented ecosystems, including marine and island ecosystems, rivers, wetlands, estuaries and coastal zones, and seek, as appropriate, to align terrestrial ecological corridors with riverine and inland water networks, in support of restoring ecological integrity and connectivity across landscapes and seascapes.]
column4: 2. 促進退化生態系之復育[於保護區與保育共生地，在適用情況下承認原住民族與傳統領地內]及其以外區域，包括緩衝區、生態廊道、土壤生物多樣性[[包括]真菌生物多樣性，7]及內陸水域生態系，旨在復育跨陸域與海域景觀之生態完整性與生態連結性，包括透過制定識別優先復育區域之標準以及衡量復育成功之方法，並在適當情況下確保復育工作之執行具包容性且具性別回應性。[2.bis 在目前代表性不足之生態系（包括海洋與島嶼生態系、河流、濕地、河口及沿岸地帶）擴大生態連結性措施，並在適當情況下，尋求使陸域生態廊道與河川及內陸水域網路一致，以支持復育跨陸域與海域景觀之生態完整性與連結性。]

Enhance guidance related to the recognition, respect, promotion and protection of indigenous and traditional territories, where applicable, in the context of Target 3 of the Framework, in a manner consistent with the programme of work on Article 8(j) and other provisions of the Convention related to indigenous peoples and local communities. This encompasses differentiated approaches to ensure comprehensive protection, including for indigenous peoples in voluntary isolation and initial contact, in line with the principles of no contact, intangibility and precaution, in accordance with national circumstances. 6. Increase the uptake of practical frameworks, guidance, emerging innovative tools, case studies and national experiences, lessons learned and different approaches to support the implementation of Target 3 of the Framework, including the definition and prioritization of areas of particular importance for biodiversity, ecological networks, corridor design for climate adaptation, large‑scale ecological connectivity, including ecological processes below ground, other effective area-based conservation measures and transboundary conservation. 7. Strengthen inclusive monitoring, reporting and evaluation systems [for protected areas and other effective area-based conservation measures, recognizing indigenous and traditional territories, where applicable], including by identifying available tools, and facilitate the use of relevant new technologies to better assess ecological representativeness, integrity and connectivity, biodiversity outcomes, management effectiveness, governance quality, species population trends, relevant indicators of the monitoring framework, as well as relevant disaggregated indicators. 9. Promote the use of relevant and new approaches for ecological integrity and connectivity in the planning and management [of protected areas and other effective area-based conservation measures, recognizing indigenous and traditional territories, where applicable], including through the development of ecological networks, ecological corridors, stepping stones and transboundary connectivity initiatives
